decisions.reason: A naval vessel lighting system is a specialist, certification-heavy product line with high sunk engineering and qualification costs and long defense procurement cycles, so weak early results can be put down to slow adoption.
The desk lamp line has its own page, a visible public commitment, and it fits the firm's announced ergonomic and human-centric direction, so management will persist with it.
The general interior luminaire line is presented on its own page and sits at the core of the firm's LED and buildings business, making it central to strategy and unlikely to be dropped.
This single pendant model is only mentioned on the website and shows less commitment, but its microprismatic optics fit the ergonomic, standards-compliant positioning, so it is likely kept for now.

HMI searchlights rely on older lamp technology that conflicts with the firm's LED direction, but the marine certification already invested and existing customer commitments argue for keeping the line a while longer.
The marine searchlight line is part of the firm's specialist robust-lighting portfolio with sunk certification costs, and slow marine demand can be read as temporary, so it is retained.
